required_fixes: Replace synthetic hardcoded TASK_CORPUS (32 tasks in run_experiment.py) with mechanism definitions from existing SPIDER registry/task corpus as required by spec.json measurement_validity[0] and prereg.md Data Sources; current data_sources.task_corpus is synthetic/representative, not registry-derived, so the tested population does not match the frozen claim about 'existing SPIDER task corpus'

Replace heuristic infer_parameterized_url() regex induction with the actual kernel distill_parameterized() / _extract_varying_values() pipeline or justify equivalence; current heuristic is not the product mechanism under test and contains a stale-index bug producing malformed templates (e.g., https://pm.example.com/orgs/${item_0}/project${item_1}00 instead of .../projects/${item_1}) that invalidates token counts for 2 of 25 parameterized mechanisms

Repair C5 NULL-NO-SHARING control: current run_experiment.py lines 695-698 computes null_ratio as self-ratio (search_param_tokens/search_param_tokens) and hardcodes c5_pass=True. Must compute true isolated null ratio = sum(search_param_tokens)/sum(search_literal_tokens) and test against frozen expected_behavior 'Deduplication ratio approximately 1.0'. True ratio is 104/83=1.253, not ~1.0, so C5 as specified fails and indicates per-unique-pattern token penalty, not neutrality

Repair C4 POS-CONTROL-TASK-SHARING to test binding correctness, not just count collapse; collapsing GET /posts/{id} 5->1 is necessary but not sufficient — must verify that bound_action for each of the 5 concrete IDs resolves correctly via kernel _bind()/_template_slots() rather than counting pattern keys

Fix alphanum regex coverage for single-letter prefix IDs: pattern [A-Z]{2,}-[A-Za-z0-9]{2,} misses /users/u-aaa type IDs (1-char prefix), leaving 5 admin-view-user mechanisms unparameterized. Expanding to detect this class changes param count from 25 to 21 and param tokens from 679 to ~599-601, materially changing deduplication ratio from 0.8584 to ~0.757 and net savings from 112 to ~192 tokens. Decision depends on which induction is product-representative

Add end-to-end cost measurement or explicitly bound claim to storage-token cost only: current token_costs measure JSON-serialized action_template storage (sum of unique mechanism tokens). Spec product_consequence requires evidence for amortized retrieval/verification/repair offset, but provenance.json confirms 'no browser/model/network calls' and validity_notes admit retrieval cost not measured. Token savings at rest do not imply amortized workflow savings

validity_findings.finding: spec.json measurement_validity[0] and prereg.md require mechanisms from existing SPIDER registry/task corpus (not synthetic). Producer uses hardcoded synthetic TASK_CORPUS (32 tasks across 6 domains) in run_experiment.py and records provenance.json data_sources.registry='in-memory (no persistent registry files)' and task_corpus='synthetic/representative'. This is a direct violation of the frozen measurement_validity contract, limiting external validity to a synthetic population

Parameter induction uses heuristic regex (infer_parameterized_url + build_action_template_full) not the kernel distill_parameterized(). Producer validity_notes and provenance reproducibility_notes acknowledge this. Token overhead and sharing counts therefore reflect heuristic design choices (slot naming, numeric/alphanum patterns, query param parameterization) not the shipped product mechanism. Results are hypothesis-generating for deduplication concept, not validation of kernel behavior

Heuristic has stale-index bug: loop over alphanum_pattern.finditer(template) while mutating template with stale match.start/end from original string. For /orgs/org-100/projects/proj-200, first replacement shortens string, second replacement uses stale index 45-53 and produces malformed https://pm.example.com/orgs/${item_0}/project${item_1}00 instead of correct .../projects/${item_1}. Token count for this pattern is 30 vs correct 29; POST variant 42 vs 41. Bug affects both pm-view-project patterns (2 tasks sharing) and pm-create-task, but impact on dedup ratio is small (1-2 tokens). Recomputed raw_evidence.json parameterized_mechanisms confirms malformed entries

C5 null_control is degenerate. Code computes search_param_tokens correctly but then computes null_ratio as search_param_tokens/search_param_tokens (self-ratio) and sets c5_pass=True unconditionally. True isolated null ratio for the 3 search tasks is (31+42+31)/(26+31+26)=104/83=1.253 (>1.0), indicating a 25.3% token penalty for unique patterns due to ${slot} overhead, contradicting spec expected_behavior 'ratio ~1.0'. Under a correct test, C5 would FAIL, triggering FALSIFIED-IN-SETTING per frozen decision_rule ALL-must-pass, though the failure reflects spec expectation misalignment (unique patterns should show penalty, not neutrality)

validity_findings.finding: Token costs measure storage of all unique mechanisms (sum over distinct URLs/patterns) via tiktoken cl100k_base on json.dumps(action_template, sort_keys=True). This conflates registry storage with per-query retrieval cost. In practice retrieval fetches only relevant mechanisms, so deduplication benefit depends on retrieval fan-out, not total registry size. Producer validity_notes[4] and prereg.md Scope Limitations acknowledge this, but report.md Product Consequence implies 14.16% savings justifies end-to-end measurement without quantifying retrieval economics. Claim ceiling must be limited to static storage, not amortized workflow

Per-task savings (raw_evidence.json per_task_savings) show parameterized costs MORE per task for shared patterns that drive corpus savings: blog-read-post 5 tasks each -15.79% (19->22), pm-view-project -15.38% (26->30). Net corpus savings arise solely from storing pattern once vs N times, not from per-mechanism efficiency. Producer observations[3] note this, but controls C1-C3 report only aggregate savings without disclosing that 5 of 32 tasks pay per-task penalty to achieve corpus reduction. This is not falsification, but weakens product interpretation that deduplication 'offsets per-mechanism penalty' — it amortizes it across copies, at cost of per-task overhead

Heuristic alphanum pattern requires [A-Z]{2,} before dash, so /users/u-aaa (single-letter prefix) is not recognized as parameterizable. 5 admin-view-user literals remain separate (5*20 tokens) vs correct collapsed form 1*22 tokens (if properly parameterized as /users/${id}). Producer observations[5] notes this as understating deduplication potential. If corrected, param count drops 25->21, param tokens 679->599, dedup ratio 0.8584->0.757, net savings 112->192 (14.16%->24.27%). Direction unchanged, magnitude underestimated. Fix requires decision whether u-aaa class is product-representative

baseline_findings.finding: Baselines B-LITERAL-REGISTRY and B-PARAMETERIZED-REGISTRY are simply the two conditions under comparison, not strong alternatives. No competitive baseline such as literal-with-compression, registry-size-only, or retrieval-filtered cost is tested. The only discriminating controls are C4 (positive) and C5 (null), both degenerate as above

Null control expectation of ratio ~1.0 is miscalibrated. True baseline for no-sharing should be ratio >1.0 reflecting template overhead (observed 1.253 for search). The experiment therefore lacks a baseline that isolates overhead from deduplication. A proper baseline would measure per-unique-pattern overhead separately from sharing-driven savings, e.g., literal vs param cost for singleton patterns

No baseline for retrieval efficiency, verification or repair cost — the exact costs invoked in spec product_consequence_positive ('real agent infrastructure') and C-PRODUCT-ECON definition ('after retrieval, verification and maintenance'). Static token storage cannot discriminate whether fewer mechanisms actually reduce end-to-end cost. Parent handoff unknown explicitly lists this as unmeasured

claim_ceiling: REVISE — Arithmetic for static storage deduplication on the as-implemented synthetic 32-task corpus is verified: 25 vs 32 mechanisms (21.9% count reduction), 679 vs 791 tokens (0.8584 dedup ratio, 112 tokens/14.16% savings) via heuristic regex induction and tiktoken cl100k_base. Maximum justified ceiling is NARROW and SYNTHETIC-ONLY: parameterized representation reduces storage-token cost across this specific hardcoded corpus because 3 of 25 patterns are shared (5x, 3x, 2x), amortizing per-task overhead (-15.8% per shared task) via single storage. This does NOT establish: (a) reduction across the existing SPIDER task corpus/registry (not tested, measurement_validity[0] violated); (b) per-mechanism token efficiency (per-task penalty persists); (c) retrieval/verification/repair amortized savings (not measured, provenance no browser/model/network); (d) general sharing frequency in real workflows (only 12% of patterns shared, 88% singleton); (e) production induction quality (heuristic != kernel, plus malformed pm templates and admin under-parameterization). Under a correct null-control test (isolated ratio 1.253, not ~1.0) the frozen ALL-must-pass decision_rule would be FALSIFIED-IN-SETTING on C5, though this reflects a mis-specified null expectation (unique patterns should show penalty). No inference to C-PRODUCT-ECON commercial viability warranted beyond justifying a future end-to-end measurement with real corpus and kernel induction.
